text:
Noah: hey all, day 1 here. i'm trying to run a quick inference smoke test that needs to impersonate a service account in the shared-services project (sa-inference@shared-services.iam.gserviceaccount.com) but `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=...` fails with permission error. billing linked, project created under folders/920011. any idea?
Marta (cloud-onboarding): welcome Noah! paste the exact error and project id. impersonation usually needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA for your principal (or a group you're in).
Noah: error: 
ERROR: (gcloud.auth.print-access-token) Permission denied: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken. The caller does not have permission 
project: proj-noah-day1
Noah: i tried `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy sa-inference@shared-services.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=shared-services` but got denied there too.
Infra Bot: Common checks: 1) ensure your principal (user or group) has `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the service account; 2) verify org policy `constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` isn't preventing cross-project bindings; 3) view effective IAM: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy shared-services --flatten=bindings`
DevOps - Ana: hey Noah  looks like the shared-services SAs are tightly scoped. Marta, can you confirm if new hires auto-get a group mapping to impersonate SAs for non-prod?
Marta (cloud-onboarding): new hires should be in okta group `redwood-devs` which is allowed to impersonate certain dev SAs. sometimes the mapping wasn't applied. Noah, can you confirm `gcloud auth login` and `gcloud config list account` show your okta SAML principal?
Noah: `gcloud config list account` shows noah@redwood.com. i'm in okta but not sure group membership.
Priya (billing): billing is linked: linkedBillingAccount: 01M2-N3O4-P5Q6 for proj-noah-day1. that should be fine. Impersonation is separate from billing.
DevOps - Ana: while Marta checks Okta, can you try `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy sa-inference@shared-services.iam.gserviceaccount.com` again and paste the bindings (if any)?
Noah: tried, same permission denied when targeting shared-services.
Marta (cloud-onboarding): Okta shows you weren't added to `redwood-devs` due to a recent onboarding race. I'll add you and trigger the SAML sync. Should take a few minutes to propagate.
Noah: thanks. in parallel, i also need access to a KMS key in europe-west1 (projects/shared-services/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/infer-kr/cryptoKeys/infer-key) because our inference client fetches encrypted model config. when i run `gcloud kms keys versions access-metadata` it fails with PERMISSION_DENIED. might be related.
Nora (security): KMS keys in shared-services are protected: we require `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` and a key-level IAM binding. Also we have an org policy that denies key usage from outside certain projects unless the project is listed in allowedMembers. We'll need a justification for cross-project KMS decryption. What's the data sensitivity?
Noah: non-prod model configs, synthetic test data only. short-term need is 3 days to run latency tests from europe.
DevOps - Ana: two parallel paths: 1) temporary role grant for your principal with `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the SA and `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the key for 72h, or 2) we can create a proxy service account in your project and add it to the key policy so your job can run without cross-project SA impersonation. Which do you prefer?
Noah: proxy SA in proj-noah-day1 sounds cleaner long-term, but temp grant would unblock me faster. whatever is less hoops.
Marta (cloud-onboarding): i'll open an access request. please provide manager approval in-thread and the exact principals. Also note the org `allowedPolicyMemberDomains` blocks external principals like `user:someone@external.com` from being added, but internal okta users are fine.
Noah: manager approved: "approve cross-project SA impersonation and KMS access for noah for 72h for non-prod testing."
DevOps - Ana: opened ticket ACC-2065-12 to grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on sa-inference@shared-services to noah@redwood.com for 72h and ticket KMS-2065-13 to add noah@redwood.com as a member with `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the key for 72h. pinging @Nora for security approval.
Nora (security): approved under conditions: 1) mark project proj-noah-day1 with label `env=non-prod,datarisk=low`, 2) ensure no PII or customer data used, 3) tickets expire automatically. Once applied, remove access early if policy checks fail.
Marta (cloud-onboarding): labels set: `gcloud projects update proj-noah-day1 --update-labels=env=non-prod,datarisk=low`.
DevOps - Ana: grants applied. try the impersonation again: `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-inference@shared-services.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and then KMS decrypt test: `gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=enc.txt --location=europe-west1 --keyring=infer-kr --key=infer-key --plaintext-file=plain.txt`
Noah: ran the commands  impersonation token now returns, KMS decrypt works. tests proceed. thanks everyone!
Marta (cloud-onboarding): notes for onboarding playbook: add explicit SA impersonation steps, Okta group sync troubleshooting, and KMS cross-project policy checklist. Noah, please delete any test plaintext files and post here when done so we can revoke early if needed.
Noah: will clean up and report back once finished. really appreciate the rapid help. :thumbsup:
